## `EnumTable`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.MasterData.EnumTable` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

One game enum, as data: the member names and their numbers, as declared by the pinned game build.

The tables exist because `ModLoader.Core` must not reference `Assembly-CSharp`, yet a content pack has to be able to write `"command": "VoiceText"` and have that checked before the game ever sees it. Parsing therefore happens here against a table, and the adapter casts the resulting number to the real enum.

<a id="enumtable--ctor"></a>

Creates a table.

**Parameters**

- `typeName`: The game type this mirrors, e.g. `Bulbul.MasterData.CommandType`.
- `members`: Member name/number pairs in declaration order. A number may repeat (the game's `ScenarioType` has an alias); the first name wins for [`EnumTable.TryName`](#enumtable--tryname).

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentException`: `typeName` is blank, or a name repeats.
- `ArgumentNullException`: `members` is null.

## `ISubtitleLookup`

interface · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.MasterData.ISubtitleLookup` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Text for a localization id in a language the game itself does not have.

The game's own `LocalizationData` has exactly seven text columns (Ja, En, ZhHans, ZhHant, Pt, Ko, Ru - plus the voice name) and no room for another, so a language a pack declares cannot live there. The pack ships `data/subtitles/<lang>.json` instead, and the text seam asks this lookup first, falling back along the language's declared chain when there is no entry.

<a id="masterdatabaseline"></a>

## `MasterDataBaseline`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.MasterData.MasterDataBaseline` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

What the game already has, reduced to the only thing the merge needs to know: which ids exist, and - for novel rows - how many times.

The count matters because the game's own `NovelMaster` is *not* unique by id: 26 of its 2289 rows share an id with another row (observed in the game's NovelMaster data). Overriding such an id would have to guess which of the rows was meant, so the merge refuses it and says so.

## `MasterDataEnums`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.MasterData.MasterDataEnums` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

The four game enums a master-data pack can name, as [`EnumTable`](#enumtable)s.

These match the game's own enums in game v1.17.2 - each table names its game type - so that a pack can write `"command": "VoiceText"` and be told, off the engine and in a unit test, whether that is a real member. If a game update renumbers a member these tables go stale, which is the same failure the patch-target registry reports for methods; update them when the game's enums change.

<a id="masterdataenums--tryparsecommand-string-scenariocommandregistry-ref-int"></a>

### `static bool TryParseCommand(string token, ScenarioCommandRegistry registry, out int value)`

As [`MasterDataEnums.TryParseCommand`](#masterdataenums--tryparsecommand-string-ref-int), against a given registry (tests).

**Parameters**

- `token`: The token as written in the pack.
- `registry`: The script-command registry.
- `value`: The command number, or 0.

<a id="masterdataenums--tryparsecommand-string-ref-int"></a>

### `static bool TryParseCommand(string token, out int value)`

Resolves a novel row's `Command` token: a member of [`MasterDataEnums.Command`](#masterdataenums--command) (name or number) first, then a CWY script command. A dotted name such as `cwy.do` or `my.mod.wave` gets its number in 5000-5999 from [`ScenarioCommandRegistry.Shared`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Scenario.md#scenariocommandregistry--shared) - reserved on first sight, so a row parsed before the mod that handles it has loaded still points at the right command. A number in 5000-5999 is accepted only when it is a built-in or already handed out.

[`MasterDataEnums.Command`](#masterdataenums--command) itself stays the game's 50 members, so everything that lists or counts the game's enum is unchanged. The pack parser calls this for the `Command` column.

**Parameters**

- `token`: The token as written in the pack (name or decimal text).
- `value`: The command number, or 0.

**Returns:** True when the token names a game command or a script command.

<a id="masterdatafingerprint"></a>

## `MasterDataFingerprint`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.MasterData.MasterDataFingerprint` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

A stable short string over the packs' master-data files, used to answer one question: has anything a pack ships actually changed since the last injection?

It exists because `PackManager.PacksResolved` fires on every rescan - the smoke runner and the texture feature both rescan - and re-injecting identical rows is wasted work and a repeated log line. Comparing fingerprints turns that into one Debug line.

The hash is FNV-1a 64 over the file contents themselves rather than over file timestamps and sizes: it is the only form that cannot be fooled by an edit that keeps the length, needs no filesystem access (so it is testable off-engine), and the files are a few kilobytes at most. The pack count and the total length are carried alongside the hash, so an accidental collision would also have to match both.

This is a change detector, not a security primitive. It answers "did the bytes move?", and nothing trusts it with anything else.

<a id="masterdatafingerprint--empty"></a>

### `const string Empty = "p0:l0:cbf29ce484222325"`

The fingerprint of no packs at all.

<a id="masterdatafingerprint--compute"></a>

### `static string Compute(IEnumerable<MasterDataPackInput> packs)`

The fingerprint of a set of packs, in the order given. Order matters: the same files in a different pack order are a different merge, because a later pack overrides an earlier one.

**Parameters**

- `packs`: The packs' files; null entries are skipped, null itself is [`MasterDataFingerprint.Empty`](#masterdatafingerprint--empty).

**Returns:** A short, stable, printable string, e.g. `p1:l842:3f2a1c9d0e5b7a64`.

<a id="masterdatamerge"></a>

## `MasterDataMerge`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.MasterData.MasterDataMerge` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Merges every installed pack's master-data files into one set, in pack order.

The rules, in full:

- Packs are applied in the order they are given, which is `PackManager`'s dependency order. A later pack's row replaces an earlier pack's row with the same id, and that is counted as a [`MasterDataFileReport.PackOverrides`](#masterdatafilereport--packoverrides) - not an error.
- A row whose id the game already has *overrides* it; a row with a new id is *added*. A row replaces the game's row whole: a localization override that only sets `En` leaves the other languages empty, it does not merge column by column.
- A novel row whose id names more than one row in the game's own data is refused, because there is no way to tell which one was meant (see [`MasterDataBaseline`](#masterdatabaseline)).
- Parse rejections are carried through untouched, so one bad row never costs a pack its good ones.

<a id="masterdatamerge--localizationkind"></a>

### `const string LocalizationKind = "localization"`

Kind label of the localization file, as it appears in the log line.

<a id="masterdatamerge--novelkind"></a>

### `const string NovelKind = "novel"`

Kind label of the novel file.

<a id="masterdatamerge--scenariogroupskind"></a>

### `const string ScenarioGroupsKind = "scenario_groups"`

Kind label of the scenario-group file.

<a id="masterdatamerge--subtitleskind"></a>

### `const string SubtitlesKind = "subtitles"`

Kind label of the subtitle tables.

<a id="masterdatamerge--merge"></a>

### `static MasterDataSet Merge(IEnumerable<MasterDataPackInput> packs, MasterDataBaseline baseline = null)`

Merges the packs' files against what the game already has.

**Parameters**

- `packs`: The packs' files, in load order; null entries are skipped and null itself is an empty merge.
- `baseline`: The game's own ids, so a row can be classified as added or overridden. Null means [`MasterDataBaseline.Empty`](#masterdatabaseline--empty), i.e. everything counts as added - which is what a unit test wants and what the adapter uses before the game has loaded.

<a id="masterdatapackparser"></a>

## `MasterDataPackParser`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.MasterData.MasterDataPackParser` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Reads the three master-data files a content pack may ship and turns them into rows.

Every file is a JSON *array* of objects. Member names are the game's own column names matched case-insensitively, so `ID`, `Id` and `id` are the same member and `ScenarioGroupID` and `scenarioGroupId` are too. A member the schema does not know is refused - a typo must not fail silently - unless its name starts with [`MasterDataPackParser.ExtensionPrefix`](#masterdatapackparser--extensionprefix), which is reserved for a pack's own notes and is ignored.

Nothing here throws for bad content. A malformed document, a row that is not an object, a missing id: each becomes a [`MasterDataRejection`](#masterdatarejection) naming the file and the row index, and the rest of the file still loads.

<a id="masterdatapackparser--extensionprefix"></a>

### `const string ExtensionPrefix = "x-"`

Member-name prefix reserved for a pack's own annotations; never validated.

<a id="masterdatapackparser--localizationfile"></a>

### `const string LocalizationFile = "data/localization.json"`

Pack-relative path of the localization file.

<a id="masterdatapackparser--novelfile"></a>

### `const string NovelFile = "data/novel.json"`

Pack-relative path of the novel file.

<a id="masterdatapackparser--scenariogroupsfile"></a>

### `const string ScenarioGroupsFile = "data/scenario_groups.json"`

Pack-relative path of the scenario-group file.

<a id="masterdatapackparser--parselocalization"></a>

### `static MasterDataParse<LocalizationRow> ParseLocalization(string json, string file)`

Parses `data/localization.json`.

**Parameters**

- `json`: File contents; null or blank is reported as an empty file.
- `file`: Display path used in rejections, e.g. `cwy.example/data/localization.json`.

<a id="masterdatapackparser--parsenovel"></a>

### `static MasterDataParse<NovelRow> ParseNovel(string json, string file)`

Parses `data/novel.json`.

**Parameters**

- `json`: File contents; null or blank is reported as an empty file.
- `file`: Display path used in rejections.

<a id="masterdatapackparser--parsescenariogroups"></a>

### `static MasterDataParse<ScenarioGroupRow> ParseScenarioGroups(string json, string file)`

Parses `data/scenario_groups.json`.

**Parameters**

- `json`: File contents; null or blank is reported as an empty file.
- `file`: Display path used in rejections.

<a id="masterdatarejection"></a>

## `MasterDataRejection`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.MasterData.MasterDataRejection` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

One thing a pack asked for that was refused, and why. A rejection is never fatal: the rest of the file still loads, and the reason is logged and put in the smoke report so the modder can see exactly which row is wrong.

<a id="masterdatarejection--ctor"></a>

### `MasterDataRejection(string file, int index, string member, string reason)`

Creates a rejection.

**Parameters**

- `file`: Where it came from, e.g. `cwy.example/data/novel.json`. Required.
- `index`: Zero-based row index, or [`MasterDataRejection.WholeFile`](#masterdatarejection--wholefile).
- `member`: The offending member name, or null when the row as a whole is at fault.
- `reason`: What is wrong, in the modder's terms. Required.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentException`: `file` or `reason` is blank.

<a id="masterdatarejection--wholefile"></a>

### `const int WholeFile = -1`

[`MasterDataRejection.Index`](#masterdatarejection--index) value meaning "the file as a whole", not one row.

The file the rejected content came from.

<a id="masterdatarejection--index"></a>

### `int Index { get; }`

Zero-based row index within that file, or [`MasterDataRejection.WholeFile`](#masterdatarejection--wholefile).

<a id="masterdatarejection--member"></a>

### `string Member { get; }`

The offending member, or null.

<a id="masterdatarejection--reason"></a>

### `string Reason { get; }`

Why it was refused.

<a id="masterdatarejection--tostring"></a>

### `override string ToString()`

## `NovelRow`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.MasterData.NovelRow` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

One row of `data/novel.json`: a single command in a scenario group - a line of dialogue, a motion change, a wait, the end of the group.

Mirrors `Bulbul.MasterData.NovelData`. The three enum-typed columns are held as the numbers the game stores, parsed by name or number against [`MasterDataEnums`](#masterdataenums); the adapter casts them back to the game enums.

The defaults are the neutral values the game's own rows use for a row that does nothing special (`"0"` string args, `-1` motions, look speed 1 s), taken from the game's own NovelMaster rows.

<a id="novelrow--arg1"></a>

### `string Arg1 { get; init; }`

First argument; meaning depends on [`NovelRow.Command`](#novelrow--command). For `VoiceText` it is parsed as an int and `"1"` means "move her mouth" (`ScenarioReader`).

<a id="novelrow--arg2"></a>

### `float Arg2 { get; init; }`

Second argument, numeric.

<a id="novelrow--arg3"></a>

### `string Arg3 { get; init; }`

Third argument.

<a id="novelrow--arg4"></a>

### `string Arg4 { get; init; }`

Fourth argument.

### `int BodyMotion { get; init; }`

Body animation index, or -1 to leave it alone.

<a id="novelrow--command"></a>

What the row does; a member of [`MasterDataEnums.Command`](#masterdataenums--command). Required.

<a id="novelrow--facialmotion"></a>

### `int FacialMotion { get; init; }`

Facial animation index, or -1 to leave it alone.

<a id="novelrow--id"></a>

### `string Id { get; init; }`

Row id. Required. Not unique in the game's own data - 26 ids repeat - so an override only applies when the id names exactly one game row (see `MasterDataMerge`).

<a id="novelrow--localizationid"></a>

### `string LocalizationId { get; init; }`

Id of the localization row holding this line's text and voice; `"0"` for none.

<a id="novelrow--lookeasetype"></a>

<a id="novelrow--lookscale"></a>

How far she turns to look at the camera, 0..1.

<a id="novelrow--lookspeedseconds"></a>

### `float LookSpeedSeconds { get; init; }`

How long the look tween takes, in seconds.

<a id="novelrow--scenariogroupid"></a>

Id of the scenario group this row belongs to. Required.

## `ScenarioGroupRow`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.MasterData.ScenarioGroupRow` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

One row of `data/scenario_groups.json`: a named sequence of novel rows and the rules for when the game may play it.

Mirrors `Bulbul.MasterData.ScenarioGroupData`. Defaults are the values the game's own short groups carry (`"0"` for "no localization id", `"None"` for the three condition columns), from the game's own ScenarioGroupMaster rows.

<a id="scenariogrouprow--arg1"></a>

### `string Arg1 { get; init; }`

First free-form argument.

<a id="scenariogrouprow--arg2"></a>

### `string Arg2 { get; init; }`

Second free-form argument.

<a id="scenariogrouprow--arg3"></a>

### `string Arg3 { get; init; }`

Third free-form argument.

<a id="scenariogrouprow--contenttype"></a>

### `string ContentType { get; init; }`

Extra condition name parsed by `ScenarioGroupMasterWrapper.IsContentTypeConditionOK` for Extra and Event groups, or `"None"`.

<a id="scenariogrouprow--episodenumber"></a>

### `float EpisodeNumber { get; init; }`

Order within its scenario type.

<a id="scenariogrouprow--id"></a>

### `string Id { get; init; }`

Group id, the value novel rows point at with their group id. Required; unique.

<a id="scenariogrouprow--languages"></a>

### `IReadOnlyList<string> Languages { get; init; }`

CWY member, not a game column (pack lines): the language codes this group is exclusive to, e.g. `["th"]`, as written in the pack. Null (the member is absent) means an ordinary group the game may play in every language. A group that declares languages is a *pack line*: it is screened by `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.PackLines.PackLineScreen`, injected only while the pack-lines feature is active, and offered by the game's selectors only while the game shows one of these languages. Never reaches the game's own `ScenarioGroupData`.

<a id="scenariogrouprow--playtiming"></a>

### `string PlayTiming { get; init; }`

When during a session it may play, or `"None"`.

<a id="scenariogrouprow--pool"></a>

### `string Pool { get; init; }`

CWY member, not a game column (pack lines): which pack-lines pool a language-exclusive group joins, e.g. `selftalk.time.7`. Empty means "the pool its [`ScenarioGroupRow.Scenario`](#scenariogrouprow--scenario) implies"; required only where one scenario type feeds several pools (`HeroineSelfShortTalk_CurrentTime`, `HeroineSelfShortTalk_WorkedTime`). Ignored for a group without [`ScenarioGroupRow.Languages`](#scenariogrouprow--languages).

<a id="scenariogrouprow--scenario"></a>

### `int Scenario { get; init; }`

When the game plays this group; a member of [`MasterDataEnums.Scenario`](#masterdataenums--scenario). Required - it decides which of the reader's two very different code paths runs.

<a id="scenariogrouprow--subtitlelocalizationid"></a>

### `string SubtitleLocalizationId { get; init; }`

Localization id of the group's subtitle, or `"0"`.

<a id="scenariogrouprow--titlelocalizationid"></a>

### `string TitleLocalizationId { get; init; }`

Localization id of the group's title, or `"0"` when it has none.

<a id="scenariogrouprow--unlocklevel"></a>

### `int UnlockLevel { get; init; }`

Player level required before the group is offered.

<a id="scenariogrouprow--unlockstoryepisode"></a>

### `string UnlockStoryEpisode { get; init; }`

Main-story episode that must be read first, or `"None"`.

<a id="scenariogrouprow--tostring"></a>

### `override string ToString()`

`id`.

<a id="subtitletables"></a>

## `SubtitleTables`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.MasterData.SubtitleTables` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Implements: [`ISubtitleLookup`](#isubtitlelookup)

The text tables a pack ships in `data/subtitles/<lang>.json` - one per language the game has no column for - and the [`ISubtitleLookup`](#isubtitlelookup) over them.

One file per language, named by its code - `th.json` is Thai - holding a flat JSON object of `localizationId -> text` (the text below stands in for the translated line):

```csharp
{
  "cwy_example_01_001": "Hello from the mod loader"
}
```

A flat map rather than an array of rows because a subtitle table is written by a translator working line by line, and because that shape diffs cleanly when one line changes.

<a id="subtitletables--extension"></a>

### `const string Extension = ".json"`

File extension of a subtitle table.

<a id="subtitletables--folder"></a>

### `const string Folder = "data/subtitles/"`

Pack-relative folder every subtitle table lives in.

<a id="subtitletables--count"></a>

### `int Count { get; }`

Total number of entries across every language.

<a id="subtitletables--empty"></a>

### `static SubtitleTables Empty { get; }`

A lookup holding nothing. Used before any pack has loaded.

<a id="subtitletables--languages"></a>

### `IReadOnlyList<string> Languages { get; }`

Language codes this lookup holds, lower-cased and ordinally sorted.

<a id="subtitletables--build"></a>

### `static SubtitleTables Build(IEnumerable<SubtitleEntry> entries)`

Builds a lookup. Entries are applied in order, so a later pack's entry replaces an earlier one for the same language and id - the same rule the master-data merge uses.

**Parameters**

- `entries`: The entries, in pack order; null means none.

<a id="subtitletables--countfor"></a>

### `int CountFor(string language)`

How many entries one language has.

**Parameters**

- `language`: A language code; matched case-insensitively.

<a id="subtitletables--idsfor"></a>

### `IReadOnlyList<string> IdsFor(string language)`

The localization ids one language has an entry for, ordinally sorted. Never null.

**Parameters**

- `language`: A language code; matched case-insensitively.

<a id="subtitletables--languageof"></a>

### `static string LanguageOf(string relativePath)`

The language code a subtitle file's path names, or null when the path is not a subtitle table. `data/subtitles/th.json` is `th`; a file in a sub-folder is refused, because a language code has no second level.

**Parameters**

- `relativePath`: A pack-relative, forward-slash path.

<a id="subtitletables--parse"></a>

### `static MasterDataParse<SubtitleEntry> Parse(string json, string file, string language)`

Parses one subtitle file. Entries come back in document order; a value that is not a string, and a blank key, are rejected individually.

**Parameters**

- `json`: File contents; null or blank is reported as an empty file.
- `file`: Display path used in rejections, e.g. `cwy.example/data/subtitles/th.json`.
- `language`: The language code, normally from [`SubtitleTables.LanguageOf`](#subtitletables--languageof).

<a id="subtitletables--tostring"></a>

### `override string ToString()`

`n row(s) in lang, lang`.

<a id="subtitletables--tryget"></a>

### `bool TryGet(string localizationId, string language, out string text)`

The text for one line in one language.

**Parameters**

- `localizationId`: The id of the line, as used in the master data.
- `language`: A language code, e.g. `th`; matched case-insensitively.
- `text`: The text, or null when there is no entry.

**Returns:** True when an entry was found.
